chapter: Chicago memories and the road to the Navy
title: Why women went for musicians
summary: Marge and Dance consider why good musicians were also pimps: women always liked musicians, who had money and glamour, as Bud Freeman's story shows.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Yes. Well why, why was it that these guys who were sort of good musicians etc., were pimps as well? I mean, how did they get into that?
I guess because women always liked musicians.
Yes, I see. They were flashy.
You know, women have always liked musicians.

And they had money. They weren't making too much money in those days, AS musicians, and the women loved them so and they'd give them money for them to be their boyfriend, you know. That's the way I figure it out. Because I don't know, the musicians always had that wd4. And the women loved musicians.
So the guys, the women sort of hung around them? They sort of made some extra money off the women?
Strange, but there was always some attraction about a musician, you know. Like now, how many women a musician can have.
Yes, well of course, I can see .....
The women will go for the musician where they won't go for a millionaire, you know.

Sure. Like Bud Freeman told us the last time we talked with him how some beautiful girl was hanging around Giants of Jazz in the end when the night ended, you know. And said, Jerry's the (aint he?) I was the one she wanted. (LAUGHTER).
Yes, and he was kind of surprised.
Yes. (Where the scene was and young you know). And she was beautiful you know and he was the one that took her home. Women, I don't know, they just always had an attraction.
